standard_prerequisites.name: The sentence C(M,w,n) describing a configuration
standard_prerequisites.statement: C(M,w,n) is the first-order sentence whose clauses record the state of M at time n, the square being scanned, and the contents of the finitely many relevant tape squares at time n, as defined in the author's definition immediately before the counted lemma.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof reads the clauses Q_q(m,n) and S_sigma(m,n) out of C(M,w,n) at source lines 1661-1663.

standard_prerequisites.name: The sentence E(M,w) expressing that M halts
standard_prerequisites.statement: E(M,w) is the existential sentence saying that there are a time and a square at which M is in a state q scanning a symbol sigma with delta(q,sigma) undefined.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof exhibits the pair (q,sigma) as one of the disjuncts of E(M,w) at source lines 1665-1672.

core_obligations: Unpack the machine-level hypothesis: from the fact that M run on w is in a halting configuration after n steps, extract a state q, a square m and a symbol sigma such that after n steps M is in state q scanning square m, on which sigma appears, and delta(q,sigma) is undefined (source lines 1654-1660).
Locate the corresponding clauses inside C(M,w,n): identify Q_q(m,n) and S_sigma(m,n) among the clauses of the configuration sentence (source lines 1661-1663).

Evaluate the entailment into E(M,w): show that the two clauses imply the disjunction over all pairs (q',sigma') with delta undefined, using that the exhibited pair (q,sigma) is one of those pairs (source lines 1663-1672).

proof_roadmap.step: From the halting configuration extract the state, the scanned square, the symbol and the undefined transition.
Identify the two configuration clauses Q_q(m,n) and S_sigma(m,n) inside C(M,w,n) and state that they imply E(M,w).
Display the existential disjunction of E(M,w) and justify the entailment by the membership of the pair (q,sigma) in the set X of undefined transitions.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lem:halt-config-implies-halt at source lines 1648-1651: if the machine M run on input w is in a halting configuration after n steps, then the sentence C(M,w,n) describing that configuration entails the sentence E(M,w) which expresses that M has halted. The proof at source lines 1653-1673 has to pass between three different levels of description: the machine-level fact that a halting configuration exists, the first-order sentence C(M,w,n) which encodes a whole tape configuration by its clauses, and the existential disjunction E(M,w) over the pairs (q,sigma) for which delta(q,sigma) is undefined. The work is to pick the state q, the square m and the symbol sigma realised at time n, read off the two clauses Q_q(m,n) and S_sigma(m,n) inside C(M,w,n), and then show that these two clauses are one of the disjuncts of E(M,w) precisely because delta(q,sigma) is undefined. Nothing in the statement spells out that C(M,w,n) contains those two clauses or that the disjunction in E(M,w) is taken over exactly the undefined-transition pairs, so the reader has to supply that bookkeeping. No result outside the retained text is used.

compared.difference: lem:halt-if-valid (statement 1861-1864, proof 1866-1894) goes in the opposite direction: it assumes the validity of T(M,w) implies E(M,w) and builds the Lang L_M-structure M with domain Nat to show that M really halts. Our candidate assumes a halting configuration and derives an entailment between the two author sentences; the arguments have different objects and neither implies the other as a card.

lem:config (statement 1681-1685) states the complementary entailment T(M,w) entails C(M,w,n), which describes the configuration at every time before halting. Our candidate starts from the configuration sentence rather than producing it.
